brief: Real-time dispatch and fleet routing platform for regional freight carriers to cut fuel usage and track shipments.

questions.text: Why is this a priority right now?
Who will use this product, and roughly how many people?
What already exists and what this must connect to, such as payments, email, or other software?
Is the deadline fixed, and what happens if it slips?
What does success look like in 3 to 6 months?

chunks:
[1] Dave (client): Thanks everyone for joining. As you know, diesel prices spiked twenty percent this quarter, so reducing deadhead miles is our highest company priority right now.
[2] Elena (internal): Makes complete sense Dave.
[3] Elena (internal): In terms of current fleet scale, who will be dispatching and driving?
[4] Marcus (client): Right now, uh, we have twelve central dispatchers and eighty-five full-time long-haul drivers across our Midwest depots.
[5] Elena (internal): What about existing software systems that the routing engine must connect to?
[6] Dave (client): Our telemetry runs on Samsara hardware, and all carrier billing is in McLeod LoadMaster. We must pull GPS pings from Samsara REST API every sixty seconds.
[7] Marcus (client): Also, we reached a final decision this morning: drivers will not have an offline mode in version one. Cellular connectivity is mandatory for all tablets.

[8] Elena (internal): When does the new dispatch optimizer need to go live?
[9] Dave (client): We have a hard cutoff of January 15 before our annual carrier contract renewals. If we miss January 15, we risk penalties with regional shippers.
[10] Elena (internal): Got it, January 15 is the firm target.
[11] Dave (client): I will email you the Samsara API keys and sample webhook payloads by tomorrow.
[12] Marcus (client): And I will export the McLeod LoadMaster data schema and past route logs by Wednesday.
[13] Elena (internal): Thanks Marcus. I will draft our data ingestion pipeline specification and send it over by Thursday.
[14] Dave (client): Sounds like a solid plan. Talk soon.
